quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #9
										  					
  

25 Questions • Passing Score 18

questions.question: What does a flashing yellow traffic light mean?

options.text: Merging traffic
Slow down and be careful.
Pedestrian crossing
Come to a full stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and be careful.
questions.explanation: A flashing yellow light means you should drive carefully and be ready to stop.

questions.question: A passenger in a moving vehicle cannot:

options.text: Use a cell phone.
Sleep.
Have an open alcohol container.
Use a map.

questions.correctAnswerText: Have an open alcohol container.
questions.explanation: It is illegal to drink from or have an open alcohol container in a moving vehicle on a public road. The driver can face serious penalties.

questions.question: When driving near a motorcycle, you should:

options.text: Give the motorcycle a full lane.
Drive on the shoulder next to the motorcycle.
Let the motorcycle share half a lane with you.
Pass the motorcycle in the same lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Give the motorcycle a full lane.
questions.explanation: Motorcycles are full-size vehicles with the same road rights as other vehicles. Give motorcyclists the full lane width they need to stay safe and maneuver.

questions.question: What does an arrow painted on the road mean?

options.text: You may move in the direction shown if you want to.
You must move in the direction shown only if traffic lights are broken.
You must stop before moving in the direction shown.
You must move in the direction shown while following the traffic signal.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must move in the direction shown while following the traffic signal.
questions.explanation: A painted arrow tells drivers they must move in that direction. Always follow traffic signs and signals before moving in the direction of the arrow.

questions.question: To avoid hitting vehicles in your blind spots, you should:

options.text: Turn your head and look over your shoulder before changing lanes.
Adjust your rearview mirrors every few minutes.
Honk your horn before turning or changing lanes.
None of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn your head and look over your shoulder before changing lanes.
questions.explanation: Before turning or changing lanes, turn your head and glance over your shoulder in the direction you are moving. Do not rely on mirrors alone.

questions.question: A steady green light means you:

options.text: Must slow down and get ready to stop.
Must stop and check for oncoming traffic.
May go through the intersection if it is clear.
Cannot turn right.

questions.correctAnswerText: May go through the intersection if it is clear.
questions.explanation: A steady green light means you can drive through the intersection if the road is clear. You can also turn right or left on a green light unless a sign says you cannot. Always yield to other vehicles and pedestrians.

questions.question: A red arrow on a traffic light means:

options.text: Drive slowly through the intersection.
Stop and go when the road is clear.
Stop and go when the light turns green or a green arrow appears.
You can turn in the direction of the arrow.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop and go when the light turns green or a green arrow appears.
questions.explanation: A red arrow means you must stop and stay stopped. Wait until the light turns green or a green arrow appears before you go. Unless a sign says otherwise, this is the rule.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Railroad crossing.
One-way traffic.
Limited parking.
Playground ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Railroad crossing.
questions.explanation: This circular sign warns you of a railroad crossing ahead. Watch for trains and be ready to stop.

questions.question: When driving on an interstate, you should:

options.text: Stop on the shoulder if you feel tired.
Always use cruise control.
Signal, check mirrors, and check blind spots before changing lanes.
Change lanes often.

questions.correctAnswerText: Signal, check mirrors, and check blind spots before changing lanes.
questions.explanation: Always signal, check your mirrors, and check your blind spot before changing lanes or passing on an interstate. Only stop on the shoulder in an emergency. Avoid cruise control in heavy traffic or bad weather. Change lanes only when necessary.

questions.question: When should you use your high beam headlights?

options.text: When driving in the dark where you cannot see the road ahead.
In heavy fog.
When getting close to the vehicle in front of you.
When approaching oncoming traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: When driving in the dark where you cannot see the road ahead.
questions.explanation: High beam headlights let you see about 350 feet ahead. Use them in dark areas where you cannot see the road. Switch to low beams when you are within 500 feet of oncoming vehicles or within 200 feet of a vehicle ahead of you.

questions.question: Before entering a roundabout, you must slow down and yield to:

options.text: Vehicles in the roundabout.
Bicyclists in the roundabout.
Pedestrians in the roundabout.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: When entering a roundabout, you must yield to pedestrians, bicyclists, and vehicles already in the roundabout.

questions.question: Your tire blows out while driving. You should:

options.text: Slam on your brakes.
Hold your steering wheel tightly and slow to a stop.
Keep driving normally.
Turn on your emergency flashers and continue driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Hold your steering wheel tightly and slow to a stop.
questions.explanation: Do not slam on the brakes. Grip the steering wheel firmly and stay in your lane. Slowly release the accelerator. When you are moving very slowly, apply the brakes lightly and pull off the road safely.

questions.question: It is best to keep a space cushion:

options.text: Only in back of your vehicle.
Only on the left and right sides of your vehicle.
Only in front of the vehicle.
On all sides of the vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: On all sides of the vehicle.
questions.explanation: Keep a cushion of space on all sides of your vehicle. This gives you time to react to hazards. Do not crowd vehicles on your left and right sides.

questions.question: This road sign means:

options.text: Drive with caution and be ready to slow down.
Do not drive in this lane.
You must come to a complete stop and yield the right-of-way.
Slow down, be prepared to stop, and yield the right-of-way if needed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down, be prepared to stop, and yield the right-of-way if needed.
questions.explanation: This triangular sign means you must yield. Slow down as you approach the intersection. Be ready to stop. Let other vehicles, bicyclists, and pedestrians pass safely before you proceed.

questions.question: A driver entering public traffic from a driveway or private road:

options.text: Has the right-of-way.
Should yield to drivers already on the public road.
May force their way into traffic.
Can assume that other drivers will change lanes to make room.

questions.correctAnswerText: Should yield to drivers already on the public road.
questions.explanation: If you are entering traffic from a driveway or private road, yield to drivers already on the public road. Merge safely when you can.

questions.question: Refusing to take an alcohol analysis test when suspected of drunk driving:

options.text: Will result in license suspension.
Is your right and will have no negative consequences.
Is recommended.
Will just result in a fine.

questions.correctAnswerText: Will result in license suspension.
questions.explanation: When you drive a motor vehicle, you agree to a test for alcohol or drugs. If you refuse the test, your driving privileges will be suspended.

questions.question: Which of the following statements about railroad crossings is true?

options.text: It is against the law to go around lowered gates at a crossing.
You must stop at a railroad crossing when directed to do so by a flagger.
Not all railroad crossings are equipped with flashing red signals and gates.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Stop at a railroad crossing when directed by a flagger, stop sign, or warning devices like gates or flashing lights. Not all railroad crossings have these devices. It is illegal to drive around lowered railroad gates.

questions.question: Which of the following lights tells you to slow down and proceed with caution at an intersection?

options.text: A flashing yellow light
A flashing red light
A solid yellow light
A solid red light

questions.correctAnswerText: A flashing yellow light
questions.explanation: A flashing yellow light means slow down, proceed with caution, and be ready to stop.

questions.question: You may pass another vehicle:

options.text: In a curve or on a hill because the chance is small that another vehicle is coming.
By using the shoulder of the highway.
If your lane is next to a solid yellow line and the passing lane is clear ahead.
None of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: None of the above.
questions.explanation: Do not pass on hills or curves because you cannot see oncoming traffic. Never pass by driving on the shoulder. Do not pass over a solid yellow line.

questions.question: When driving near heavy trucks, other drivers must allow for:

options.text: The increased stopping distance required by large vehicles.
The decreased stopping distance required by large vehicles.
The decreased noise of larger vehicles.
The increased speed of larger vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: The increased stopping distance required by large vehicles.
questions.explanation: Heavy trucks need more distance to stop than smaller vehicles. Stay where the truck driver can see you. Do not block the truck driver's view of traffic.

questions.question: You may drive across a dashed white line:

options.text: At any time.
Only during daylight hours.
When it is safe to change lanes.
Only when passing a motorcycle.

questions.correctAnswerText: When it is safe to change lanes.
questions.explanation: Dashed white lines separate lanes going the same direction. You can cross a dashed line to change lanes if it is safe.

questions.question: Your wheels slip off the edge of the road while driving. What should you do?

options.text: Jerk the steering wheel to force the vehicle back onto the pavement.
Speed up and steer back onto the pavement gradually.
Slam on your brakes and stop.
Slow down by gently using the brakes. Turn the steering wheel to return to the pavement at a safe speed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down by gently using the brakes. Turn the steering wheel to return to the pavement at a safe speed.
questions.explanation: Keep driving with your wheels off the road and slow down gently using the brakes. When you reach a safe speed, turn the steering wheel to get back onto the pavement. Do not jerk the steering wheel sharply.

questions.question: Larger vehicles have:

options.text: Larger blind spots.
Smaller blind spots.
No blind spots.
The same blind spots as smaller vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Larger blind spots.
questions.explanation: Larger vehicles have larger blind spots. Big trucks and SUVs have areas behind them that cannot be seen in their mirrors.

questions.question: What is the most effective way to reduce your risk of injury or death in a traffic crash?

options.text: Wear your seat belt.
Limit your driving to weekdays.
Stay in the right lane on multilane highways.
Limit your driving to hours between 3:00 p.m. and 6:00 p.m.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wear your seat belt.
questions.explanation: Wearing your seat belt is the single most effective thing you can do to reduce your risk of death or injury while driving.

questions.question: This sign means:

options.text: Crossroad ahead.
Flagger ahead.
Lane ends.
Turn right or go straight.

questions.correctAnswerText: Crossroad ahead.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are usually yellow with black markings. They alert drivers to upcoming road conditions and hazards. This sign warns you that an intersection is coming.
